body:
After a lot of discussions with a couple of people in the OpenXR group there is some further clarity on these issues.

First, `xrSyncActions` is supposed to be run every frame as soon as the session is created. `XR_SESSION_NOT_FOCUSED` is returned purely as information. This gives `xrSyncActions` the chance to clear controller state when we loose focus. This means "behaviour 1" as described above, is intended behaviour.

Users should correctly react to the state change, by reacting to the [OpenXRInterface.session_visible](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_openxrinterface.html#class-openxrinterface-signal-session-visible) signal and ensure their game behaves correctly.

Behaviour 2 lies a little more difficult. The OpenXR spec does not define any dependency that governs when it's safe to call `xrGetCurrentInteractionProfile`, it should be safe to call this as soon as the session reaches the synchronised state, and we thus seem to be doing to correct thing.
So the behaviour witnessed here might indicate an issue on the runtime side that needs to be investigated further.
However, it is possible runtimes don't have access to this data until further on, and it is possible runtimes omit to providing the `XR_TYPE_EVENT_DATA_INTERACTION_PROFILE_CHANGED` event in this scenario.

There is ground for moving checking `xrGetCurrentInteractionProfile` to after `xrSyncActions` and making things a little more robust.

Behaviour 3 seems to indicate a bug on the runtime side and thus should not require a change in our approach.
